findings.title: Regression from the round-6 key-field low: a row-pair secret held in a declared key field is shown in clear, though 4ed6449 masked it
findings.evidence:
**Cause.** `const paired = pair !== null && pair.values.includes(field) && !named.includes(field)`: a pair's value field that is one of the collection's declared key fields is never masked. Its field name (`value`, `v`) doesn't match SECRET_NAME either.

**probe-lows.mjs (out-lows.txt), 4a284f9 / 4ed6449 / 4033285:**
- `tokens {key:['value'], rows:[{name:'deploy_token', value:S}]}`: CLEAR / masked / CLEAR. 4033285 shows `{"name":"deploy_token","value":"Zq9SeCr3tVal"}`.
- `settings {key:['key','value'], rows:[{key:'smtp_password', value:S}]}`: CLEAR / masked / CLEAR.
- `kv {key:['k','v'], rows:[{k:'api_token', v:S}]}`: CLEAR / masked / CLEAR.
- Controls, masked at all three heads where noted: the same settings row keyed ['id'] (masked at 4ed6449 and 4033285), and `sessions` keyed ['token'] (a named secret, masked everywhere).

The row-pair rule first appeared at 4ed6449, so this un-masks something an earlier head masked. A tokens table keyed by the token value, with a descriptive name column, is a plausible seeded shape.

**Provenance.** Round 6's verdict asked for exactly this change ('Skip the collection's key fields'), to stop a rename splitting into a red delete and an insert. README:412 documents it ('never one of the collection's key fields'), and the new test at test/data-diff.test.mjs:1574 pins it unmasked. The corpus can't see it, because its `row()` helper uses `key: null`.

Under the owner's bar, a secret in clear and a regression of what an earlier head masked are both blocking. The over-flagging it replaces (a red delete plus insert) is not. Like round 5's DSN nit, this is a reviewer-requested trade, so the orchestrator may choose to accept it explicitly.

findings.title: Regression from moving the element rule ahead of the DSN and JWT rules: three element shapes that 4ed6449 (and mostly 4a284f9) masked now show the secret
findings.evidence:
maskInText now runs URL, then scheme, then ATTR_TAG (L243), then DSN (L250), then JWT (L251). ATTR_TAG (L393) therefore reads the raw text, before DSN and JWT shorten it or remove a '<' or '>'. Field `note`, neutral collection; columns are 2ec0bba/7193877/4a284f9/4ed6449/4033285 (regress/out-repro.txt).

**E1: the 1,024-character tag bound now counts raw JWT and DSN text.**
- `<input type="password" value="Zq9SeCr3tVal" data-x="<JWT of about 1,000 characters>">` gives CLEAR/CLEAR/masked/masked/CLEAR. Head shows `value="Zq9SeCr3tVal" data-x="[secret c1302430]"`.
- Also: `<add key="ClientSecret" value="S" note="<JWT>"/>`, the unquoted `<i type=password value=S a=<JWT>>` (masked only at 4ed6449), and four 256-character DSN passwords in sibling attributes.

**E2: a DSN password holding '<' in a sibling attribute.** `<add key="DbPassword" value="Zq9SeCr3tVal" note="u:a<b@tcp(h)/d"/>` gives CLEAR/CLEAR/masked/masked/CLEAR. Earlier heads hid `a<b` first, so the tag was readable.

**E3: a DSN starting inside a secret element's value, its password across the '>'.**
- `<input type=password value=root:ab>Zq9SeCr3tVal@tcp(db)/app` gives CLEAR/CLEAR/masked/masked/CLEAR, and head shows `value=[secret e3477516]>Zq9SeCr3tVal@tcp(db)/app`;
- `<x name=secret value=u:p>Zq9SeCr3tVal@/db` is masked at 4ed6449 and CLEAR at head.

**Fuzz counts** (out-classes.txt):
- E1: 25,398 masking regressions (14,682 against 4ed6449 only, 10,716 against 4a284f9 and 4ed6449), nearly all from the biased long-attribute mode (120k cases);

authValues advances by the scheme's name only after a non-token value. After a token value it consumes the whole match (L410-411). The rescan can now start a token match on a scheme word that ends an earlier non-token value. That match swallows the next scheme word, which the old whole-match scan used. findings.fix:
Look at every scheme occurrence: after each match, token or not, set `lastIndex = m.index + scheme.length`. Collect each token value's span and hide their union. Spans can't partly overlap, since values never hold whitespace.

The cause is in 4033285 lib/data-diff.mjs:586: `const paired = pair !== null && pair.values.includes(field) && !named.includes(field)`. In 4ed6449, line 565 had no `!named` exclusion.

Attempts to refute:
1. **It was reviewer-requested.** True. Round-6 verdict-comment.md:54 says "Skip the collection's key fields", and findings.json minor[5] asks for the same. But round 6 treated the orchestrator's own round-5 DSN nit, which un-masked something, as HIGH, and its verdict names this exact pattern ("third round in which a masking fix … un-masked something an earlier head masked"). Who suggested the change doesn't take it out of the blocking class.
2. **It is documented.** README:412 says "never one of the collection's key fields". But it is not in README's "what masking misses" list (line 428 covers only a field literally named `key`). And documentation doesn't exempt a regression under the owner's bar.
3. **The corpus and the author's differential fuzz should have caught it.** They couldn't: the corpus `row()` helper uses `key: null` (test/data-masking-corpus.test.mjs:19), so the author's "0 regressions vs 4ed6449" doesn't cover this. test/data-diff.test.mjs:1574-1577 pins the value unmasked, with the message "a key field is never masked". That message is also inaccurate, since a key field named `token` is masked.
4. **It's rare.** Partly true. The README says `key` comes from the store's own schema (a primary key or a KeySchema), so a pair's value column being part of the key is uncommon (a tokens table keyed by its value, or a composite (key, value) key). That makes the realistic risk smaller, but it doesn't change the class.

Why HIGH stands: the owner's bar says any regression of something an earlier head masked is blocking, and 4ed6449 masked it. A secret is shown in clear under default rules. The trade-off is lopsided:
- 4ed6449's digest is keyed on collection, field and value, not on the pair name. So matching still works, and only a rename that switches the name between secret-looking and plain becomes a delete plus an insert.
- That over-flags and hides nothing, which is non-blocking under the bar.

The orchestrator could accept the trade explicitly, but by default this stays high.

I couldn't refute it. The head is 4033285 (fresh clone, pull/35/head).

**Code.** At 4ed6449, line 565 passed `pair !== null && pair.values.includes(field)` with no key-field exclusion. At 4033285, line 586 adds `&& !named.includes(field)`. `named` is the declared key, and the field names `value`/`v`/`Value`/`val` don't match SECRET_NAME. So `cell()` falls through to `plain()`, and a short secret passes through unmasked.

**Differential probe** (probe.mjs in my dir, lib/data-diff.mjs extracted at each head):
- At 2ec0bba, 7193877 and 4a284f9, every pair case is in clear: those heads had no row-level pair rule.
- At 4ed6449, every case is masked: `tokens {key:['value'], {name:'deploy_token', value:S}}`, `settings {key:['key','value']}`, `kv {key:['k','v']}`, `{key:['Value'], Name:'API_TOKEN'}` and `{key:['val'], field:'db_password'}`.
- At 4033285, all five of those are CLEAR. The controls are still masked: the settings row keyed ['id'] or ['key'], and `sessions` keyed ['token'].
- The secret shows in both the row and the diff's key string. At 4033285, `inserted` is `[{"key":"[\"Zq9SeCr3tVal\"]","row":{"name":"deploy_token","value":"Zq9SeCr3tVal"}}]`.

So this is a true regression against 4ed6449, not a gap that was always there. It is in the PR's own changed line, so in scope. It fits the owner's blocking class: a regression of something an earlier head masked. Precedent holds as well: round 6 rated as HIGH a regression against a rejected head (4a284f9), caused by the orchestrator's own round-5 nit.

**Two points make it worse than the claim says:**
1. The trade buys less than round 6 assumed (probe2.mjs). At 4ed6449 the digest covers the collection, field and value, not the pair's name. So renaming `deploy_token` to `ci_token` was already one update, not a delete plus an insert. The over-flag happens only when a rename toggles whether the name looks secret (`deploy_token` to `deploy_label`). Even then it is louder, never hidden, so it isn't blocking under W28=B.
2. The exclusion tests the declared key (`named`), not the key the rows actually support. When two rows share the value, the key is dropped and the rows are compared as a multiset. The exclusion then protects no matching, yet the secret still shows (my `dup_key` case: CLEAR at 4033285, masked at 4ed6449).

**Mitigations that don't refute it:**
- The shape is narrow. A pair's value field has to be part of the store's declared primary key. Real settings tables key on `id` or `key`, and those rows stay masked.
- README:412 documents the behaviour ("never one of the collection's key fields"), and test:1574 pins it. So no doc claim is wrong.
- The orchestrator asked for exactly this change in round 6.

These could support medium if the orchestrator explicitly accepts the trade. But the owner's bar has no plausibility exception, and the corpus misses this case because its `row()` helper uses `key: null`. That repeats the pattern the round-6 corpus rule was meant to stop.

**Fix.** Restore masking of a pair's value fields even when they are key fields, as 4ed6449 did. Add a corpus row with a declared key, e.g. `key: ['value']`. If the orchestrator accepts the trade instead, list it in README:419's misses.
